title: Apply to re-register a written-off light vehicle
summary: This page outlines the process and requirements for re-registering a written-off light vehicle.
intro:
To re-register a written-off light vehicle you must have first obtained an Authorisation to Repair from Transport for NSW (TfNSW).

Once repaired and certified, the vehicle must then pass these inspections:
who_can_apply: You must be aged 16 or over.
The authorised repairs must be completed on the vehicle.
The vehicle must have an Authorisation to Repair from Transport for NSW (TfNSW).
what_you_need: An Authorisation to Repair from TfNSW
A Certificate of Compliance issued by a licensed repairer
Any third-party certifications (e.g., air bag or structural certification)
An AUVIS report (blue slip), including identity, design, and safety checks

how_to_steps.text: Gather all the required documents and the number plates (if available).
Submit your application with payment at a Service NSW Centre.

more_info.text: The registration certificate for the vehicle will state that the vehicle has been reported to the NSW Written-off Light Vehicles Register.
You cannot register an interstate written-off vehicle in NSW unless it is first re-registered in another jurisdiction.

internal_links.text: Cancel the registration on a written-off vehicle

faqs.q: What must I do before I can re-register a written-off vehicle?
faqs.a: You must first obtain an Authorisation to Repair from Transport for NSW (TfNSW).

faqs.q: What inspections must the vehicle pass after repairs?
faqs.a: Once repaired and certified, the vehicle must pass inspections, including an AUVIS report and a TfNSW VIIU report.

faqs.q: Where do I submit my application to re-register the vehicle?
faqs.a: You must submit your application with payment at a Service NSW Centre.
